messages:
sanjay: Heads up — we're getting a handful of customer escalations about p95/p99 latency spikes since yesterday evening. p95 for text-generation routes jumped from ~230ms to ~1.6s and p99 up to 5–6s. Error rates are low but several traces show retry/backoff cascades. Filing here to correlate with infra metrics. Anyone seen GPU OOM/fallback noise?

maria: saw the alerts. host-gpupool-03 had several OOM events and one restart around 22:14 UTC. I pulled the node logs, looks like allocator churn + KV cache growth on long-lived chat sessions.

jun: pasted a trimmed log snippet I grabbed:```
[22:13:58] infer-runtime WARN Evicting 512MB prefetched cache to make room
[22:14:03] infer-runtime ERROR cuda out of memory: Cannot allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0)
[22:14:03] kernel   INFO  process pid=10234 killed by OOM
[22:14:10] infer-runtime INFO  fallback to cpu backend for request id=...
```

ines: that fallback to cpu explains the massive tail. once a worker falls back we see tens of seconds until it's back to GPU because queue drains and retries pile up. :exploding_head:

maria: correlating with model version — rolled 177 -> 177+2 yesterday afternoon on the pool that serves these customers. The upgrade included a new attention cache layout which increased per-request kv memory slightly. Under normal load fine, but with some long-history chats the KV growth pushes us over fragmentation threshold.

sanjay: can we reproduce quickly? ops wants repro steps to give customers.

jun: repro I used locally (on a small test cluster): 1) Spin up a runtime with model v177+2 and 8GB GPU 2) Send a stream of chat messages that append ~1k tokens per turn for 40 turns 3) Observe kv cache grow by ~1GB and fragmentation metric (gpu_mem_free drops but not contiguous) 4) eventually OOM. I have the curl script if you want.

maria: sharing the curl loop:```bash
for i in {1..40}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \\n    -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-177+2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"'"$(yes "tell me a long story" | head -n 50 | tr -d '\\n')"'"'}]}';
  sleep 0.5
done
```
(edited to keep it concise)

ines: quick mitigation that helped yesterday: 1) forced eviction of KV caches on the affected workers 2) bumped autoscale threshold to add more GPU workers 3) temporarily pinned those customers to an older model variant (rwd-chat-177) which uses smaller kv layout. After that p95 dropped back to ~300–350ms.

ops-bot: deployment rollback executed: model rwd-chat-177 pinned for pool gpupool-03 at 23:02 UTC by maria.

maria: verifying followup: after rollback we still observed a few OOMs but no tail latencies. I also triggered a migration to staggered restarts so workers get emptied before restart.

sanjay: good. what's the medium/long-term plan so this doesn't recur with other model tweaks?

jun: list I promised: - better KV accounting per-request + reject path when KV total > X% of GPU mem - allocator tunables exposed (reduce fragmentation) - periodic memory compaction hooks (when model supports) - fallback policy changes: instead of immediate CPU fallback, drain and fail fast earlier to avoid retry storms - autoscaler change: scale proactively on KV growth signals not just GPU util

ines: adding detail on allocator: current cuda allocator fragments under many small allocs. We can try switching to a mixed pool + release-to-os behavior (set `CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC=1` on supported drivers) or move to a slab allocator that merges free blocks. There's also a runtime flag `RUNTIME_GPU_COMPACTION=true` in the dev branch that does a compaction pass every N requests — it reduces fragmentation but adds a small CPU-side latency overhead.

maria: short-term patch plan: 1) expose env var to limit per-request kv (KV_MAX_TOKENS=512) for affected pools 2) enable CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC where driver supports 3) add a healthcheck that marks a worker read-only when fragmentation ratio > 0.75 4) add metric kv_bytes_total per worker to alert earlier

sanjay: owners? who will own the patch and the rollout? need an RFC?

jun: I can pick up KV accounting + alerting. ETA for a simple metric + alert rule: 24–48h.

maria: I'll own the immediate env rollout and the rollback automation for pinned customer policy. I'll open a runbook update.

ines: I'll prototype the allocator flag tests in a dev cluster and measure p95/p99 impact. Might need to involve infra team if driver versions differ across regions.

sanjay: nice. For customer communication: ops pls send a short note — we rolled them back to a stable variant and we have mitigations in flight. Include repro script so they can test.

ines: draft for support: "We've identified GPU memory fragmentation and KV-cache growth triggered by long chat histories with the new kv layout. We've temporarily pinned you to the previous model variant and deployed worker eviction policies. We're working on metric-based prevention and allocator tuning; we'll follow up with an ETA."

maria: follow-up actions (to track): - JUN: add kv_bytes_total metric + alert (48h) - INES: test CUDA_MALLOC_ASYNC in dev and report perf (72h) - MARIA: roll out KV_MAX_TOKENS env on affected pools (today) - SANJAY: review runbook + approve postmortem (72h)

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-2482 "GPU KV growth -> p99 spikes" assigned to jun, due 48h.

sanjay: thanks all. keep this thread updated with any oddities. If someone sees a new OOM on other pools, @channel to escalate.

maria: one more note — we should consider a safety gate in model onboarding: any model that increases per-request KV size by >10% gets a canary on a small pool with KV growth metrics enabled. Saves us from surprise regressions.

jun: agree. I'll include that in the RFC for KV accounting.

ines: logging note: add a compact log line when we evict KV with reason=fragmentation so SRE can alert automatically.

sanjay: perfect. closing loop: rollback helped, mitigations in flight, owners assigned. We'll re-open if p99 climbs again. :v:
